title: About Me
text:
I am a PhD student in the Population, Health and Place program at the University of Southern California. My research lies at the intersection of spatial data science, GeoAI, and population health, with a broader interest in developing computational methods that can support scientific research.
My background spans data science, geospatial analysis, machine learning, and environmental health. I received my B.S. in Data Science through the Duke Kunshan University and Duke University dual-degree program, followed by an M.S. in Spatial Data Science from the University of Southern California.
During my graduate training, I became increasingly interested in how computational methods can help us understand the relationship between people and place. My research has examined neighborhood visual environments, urban green space, spatial accessibility, remote sensing, environmental exposures, and health outcomes. Across these projects, I have worked with street-view imagery, satellite data, spatial databases, machine learning, and spatial statistical methods.
More broadly, I am interested in research problems where methodological rigor and domain understanding are equally important. I am particularly interested in how spatial data, artificial intelligence, and statistical modeling can be combined to study complex environmental and health systems, and how reliable AI methods can support scientific discovery.

title: Research
text:
A Tri-environmental GeoAI Framework for Urban Health and Environmental Exposure
Research Assistant | University of Southern California | 2024–2025
This project developed a GeoAI framework to investigate the relationship between children’s health, environmental exposures, and neighborhood characteristics.
I integrated multiple environmental dimensions, including:

Actual environment: built environment characteristics derived from spatial datasets;
Perceived environment: visual perception extracted from street-view imagery using computer vision and machine learning;
Natural environment: environmental exposure indicators derived from geospatial datasets.

I processed spatial data using Python, GeoPandas, ArcGIS Pro, and Google Earth Engine, and applied machine learning approaches to identify environmental factors associated with neighborhood perception and health-related outcomes.


Data Augmentation for Urban Tree Genus Classification
Research Assistant | University of Southern California | 2024
This project applied deep learning and machine learning methods to identify urban tree species from remote sensing imagery.
I extracted tree canopy information from NAIP satellite imagery using ArcGIS Pro and Google Earth Engine, addressed class imbalance between deciduous and evergreen species through data augmentation, and evaluated Random Forest classification performance under different augmentation strategies.


Neighborhood Visual Environment and Social Inequality
Research Assistant | University of Southern California | 2024–2025
This research investigated inequalities in neighborhood visual environments in Los Angeles.
Using street-view imagery, computer vision, and multi-model machine learning, I quantified perceived environmental characteristics, including beauty, safety, livability, and affluence.
The study identified how socioeconomic disadvantage is associated with differences in perceived neighborhood environments and analyzed key built environment features influencing human perception.


Multimodal Spatial Accessibility Analysis
Research Assistant | University of Southern California | 2024
This project investigated how multiple transportation modes can be incorporated into spatial accessibility measurement.
I analyzed different accessibility modeling approaches by considering travel mode probabilities and weighted travel costs, proposing a weighted-mean travel time framework to better represent real-world population mobility patterns.


Spatial Analysis of Stroke Prevalence and Building Density in California
Project Leader | University of Southern California | 2024
This project explored relationships between urban form and health outcomes across California census tracts.
I used GeoPandas and spatial statistical methods, including spatial autocorrelation analysis, to examine associations between building density patterns and stroke prevalence, identifying spatial trends relevant to urban health research.


High-Resolution Digital Elevation Model Generation Based on InSAR Data
Research Assistant | Wuhan University | 2025–2026
This project developed a high-precision Digital Elevation Model (DEM) generation system based on InSAR data.
I contributed to building the computational workflow, supporting data acquisition and preprocessing, and developing a public interactive website that enabled on-demand DEM generation for research applications.


Flood Resilience Analysis Using Nighttime Light Data
Research Assistant | Hong Kong Polytechnic University | 2024
This project examined flood resilience using satellite-based nighttime light observations.
I processed flood event data and VIIRS nighttime light imagery using Google Earth Engine and Python, analyzing changes in nighttime illumination before, during, and after flood events while applying statistical filtering methods to reduce noise.

title: Shaokun Lyu
text:
Research Focus

GeoAI and Spatial Intelligence
I develop data-driven approaches that combine geospatial data, remote sensing and machine learning to understand spatial environments. My work explores how AI can extract meaningful information from complex geographic systems.


Place, Environment, and Population Health
I study how places influence human health by integrating environmental data, spatial analysis, and statistical modeling. My research examines how environments, accessibility, and social conditions contribute to health disparities and urban inequality.


Computational Methods for Scientific Discovery
I am interested in developing reliable computational and AI methods that support scientific research, combining machine learning, data analysis, and domain knowledge to solve interdisciplinary problems.

title: Publications
text:
Wang, S., Yoo, J., Cai, W., Yang, F., Huang, X., Sun, Q. C., Lyu, S., & others. (2024).
Sustainable Cities and Society, 110, 105177.
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scs.2024.106062
This study investigates social inequities in neighborhood visual environments in Los Angeles by integrating street-view imagery, computer vision, and multi-model machine learning. The research develops a data-driven framework to quantify perceived neighborhood characteristics and identify environmental factors associated with visual quality disparities.




Ibrahim, M., Lyu, S., Ahmad, N., Nasir, M. J., & Wang, S. (2025).
Urban Informatics, 4, Article 19.
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1007/s44212-025-00088-6
This research examines inequalities in urban green space provision, quality, and accessibility using spatial analysis and mixed methods approaches. The study highlights how spatial disparities in green infrastructure can contribute to unequal environmental benefits across communities.




Wang, S., Lyu, S., Han, M., Chen, H., & Li, X. (2025).
Computers, Environment and Urban Systems.
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cities.2026.107043
This work investigates methods for incorporating multiple travel modes into spatial accessibility measurement. By considering travel mode probabilities and weighted travel costs, the study proposes a more realistic approach to evaluating access to healthcare facilities in urban environments.

title: Personal Website
text:
A reproducible machine learning workflow for studying the environment–disease nexus using spatial and environmental data.
The pipeline combines:

AutoML for model and pipeline selection
PCA for reducing multicollinearity
Global Random Forest modeling
Geographically weighted Random Forest for spatial heterogeneity
SHAP for feature-level interpretation
ALE for identifying nonlinear effects and thresholds
